content: Iron (II) gluconate is a mineral that has received FDA approval for the treatment of iron deficiency anemia. Common adverse reactions associated with its use include hypersensitivity. In adults, FDA-labeled indications for Iron (II) gluconate include its use during epoetin therapy for iron deficiency anemia in patients undergoing hemodialysis. There is limited information available regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported uses of Iron (II) gluconate in adult patients. For pediatric patients, there is limited information regarding FDA-labeled indications, as well as off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported uses of Iron (II) gluconate. Contraindications for Iron (II) gluconate are not well-documented in the drug label. However, warnings include the fact that accidental overdose of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under the age of six. It is crucial to keep this product out of the reach of children. In the event of an accidental overdose, immediate medical attention should be sought by contacting a doctor or poison control center. Iron (II) gluconate should not be taken within two hours of oral tetracycline antibiotics, as oral iron products can interfere with the absorption of tetracycline. Gastrointestinal discomfort, nausea, constipation, or diarrhea may occur as side effects. Pregnant or nursing individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using this product. The Consumer Product Safety Commission mandates that iron-containing medicines and vitamins be packaged with child-resistant closures, and parents should ensure these closures are properly secured. Adverse reactions from clinical trials and postmarketing experiences with Iron (II) gluconate are not extensively documented in the drug label. Similarly, there is limited information regarding drug interactions. There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of Iron (II) gluconate in populations such as pregnant women, during labor and delivery, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, specific gender or racial populations, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Additionally, there is no FDA guidance on its use in females of reproductive potential, males, or immunocompromised patients. Iron (II) gluconate can be administered orally or intravenously. However, there is limited information available regarding monitoring requirements, IV compatibility, or chronic overdose of this medication. The pharmacology of Iron (II) gluconate, including its mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology, is not well-documented in the drug label. Similarly, clinical studies and details on how the drug is supplied are limited. Iron (II) gluconate should be stored at a temperature of 20°C to 25°C (68°F to 77°F). There is limited information available regarding patient counseling and the interaction of Iron (II) gluconate with alcohol. Patients are advised to consult their doctor about the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. The brand name for Iron (II) gluconate is FERROUS GLUCONATE®. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names for Iron (II) gluconate in the drug label.
